To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The processing of social signals (i.e., facial gaze and facial expressions) interacts rather late and in complex manner to modulates spatial attention.

1) Fearful, angry and surprised faces modulate the Gaze Orienting effect; 2) Fear and surprise modulate the early ERP component P1; 3) Happiness modulates the late ERP component P1, and 4) Gaze and facial expressions modulate attention through two different ERP components.
the processing of gaze and emotional facial expressions interact rather late and influence spatial attention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of emotion in attentional processing.
the role of emotions in attentional processes.
the role of emotions on gaze orienting attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GOE is modulated by emotions in a complex manner, which is reflected by both behavioral and ERP measures.
the GOE is enhanced by fear, surprise and anger, and that happy expressions do not modulate this effect.
the attentional system is modulated by gaze and emotions, and that this interaction is complex and depends on the type of emotion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the emotional expression of the face modulates the gaze orienting effect, which itself modulates the processing of the target stimulus.
emotions modulate attentional processes, which are in turn influenced by the gaze direction of the face, and this is reflected in both behavioral and electrophysiological responses.
emotions modulate attention to gaze, but not the other way around.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emotions can influence the way we process gaze cues and orient spatial attention.
the processing of gaze and facial expression is not linear, but complex.
gaze orienting is a powerful mechanism that can be used to direct attention to a specific location in the environment.
